summary.text: Craig Zucker is a Democratic member of the Maryland State Senate from District 14 who was appointed in February 2016 and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
He served in the House of Delegates from 2011 to 2016 and chairs the Capital Budget Subcommittee of the Budget and Taxation Committee.

paragraphs.text: Zucker was born in Englewood, New Jersey, on March 23, 1975, and earned a bachelor's degree in social science, law and government from St. Thomas Aquinas College in 1997 and a master's degree in government from The Johns Hopkins University in 2004.
He held staff positions for U.S. Sens. Bill Bradley and Barbara Boxer, was legislative director to Delegate Peter Franchot, and was community liaison and grants coordinator for U.S. Rep. Albert Wynn.

He was Maryland state director of the Service Employees International Union's home care program from 2004 to 2006, deputy chief of staff in the Office of the Comptroller of Maryland from 2007 to 2010, and has been senior vice president of strategic development and government relations at Service Coordination, Inc., since 2024.
Zucker served in the House of Delegates from 2011 to 2016 and was appointed to the Senate on February 3, 2016.
He has served on the Budget and Taxation Committee since 2019 and has chaired its Capital Budget Subcommittee since 2021.
He was Deputy Majority Leader from 2019 to 2020 and Senate chair of the Spending Affordability Committee from 2020 to 2021.
He advanced from the Democratic primary on June 23, 2026.
